One. I wish I could agree with you on this point, but I can’t. Privatization leads to less access, not more. I get my power from PUD, and it’s cheaper than the private guys. Roads and bridges are very expensive and if a company has to run at profit (thus capitalism) they are got to charge not only what it takes to maintain those things, but also more than that because they must show a profit every quarter for their investors. This is not the solution, and capitalism does not belong in critical infrastructure. The day you have to pay a private fire department, and private police department to respond to your house because of an emergency, you’ll understand why capitalism has it’s place, but not with critical infrastructure and services.

Two. Talking about subsidies lacks teeth when we’re still giving the oil companies millions. If you don’t want to subsidize green energy, that’s fair. We need to make sure we subsidize no oil or natural gas companies either then. Fair is fair.

Three. If you want to scrap the programs, fine with me. But plan on the riots when millions of peoples EBT cards suddenly fail to work and remain unfunded. At this point, I honestly think we have these systems in place to keep them from making much noise. We give them just enough to stay out of sight and out of mind (for the most part). It may not be the humane thing to do, but it keeps the millions of unemployed people in this nation from making noise. You know full well that politicians would have to come up with something just to keep people pacified.

Four. I have to qualify what I say with the fact that I work for a union shop. Feel free to hate me even though you don’t know me. It seems to be all the rage in the US as of late. Yes, I’m required to pay union dues to even step through the front door of our facility. I knew this going in. The people of the US used to be slaves for corporations prior to the whole union movement. Unions forced mines to enact safety regulations that reduced accidents, and increased the likelihood of safety. That’s why you hear about mine accidents with huge numbers in other nations, but not ours. We don’t have a perfect system, but I assure you, corporations don’t care in the least about their people, they care about their productivity. When one dies, there are three to take his place, so why care? You may disagree, but history in this country is on my side on this one. Capitalism cares about profit only, never people.

Five. Minimum wage is what we all had to suffer through in high school. I did. You did. Most of the people here did. Once again, it comes down to profit. The only thing corporations and businesses care about is profit. If they can pay you seven dollars an hour less to do a job, would you do it? Nope. But some sorry bastard would, and you’d hit the bricks. Of course corporations and businesses don’t care that you have silly things like bills ( and they charge as much as possible because they can, and we’re all forced to pay it - just don’t expect any pay raises to offset the increases in prices). Minimum wage wasn’t set up to be a living wage. It was only setup to ensure that people couldn’t earn a buck an hour to do a job. As it is, people have to have multiple jobs to make ends meet now, and with both parents working, is it really any surprise that kids have no guidance to go by?

Six. I absolutely agree with you. Gender nor race has anything to do with abilities. The hiring process ought to be blind to these factors entirely.

Seven. You are aware that it’s the very corporations you’re talking about whom wrote those treaties, right? You don’t actually think the politicians are smart enough to come up with this stuff. The corporations enact treaties to give themselves advantages so that they can make more money, or pay less taxes, or both.

Eight. Education is a tricky beast. When it comes down to it, prisons are loaded up primarily with under-educated people. There are smart ones in there too, but they are few and far between. Education does need to have the money taken out of it, and we ought to start with the coaches at universities. These hypocrites say that their college students can’t receive any funding, or special benefits, but they, themselves, are paid millions. There’s your capitalism for you. The colleges pay that much because they demand that much for their services should the school want a better chance at a winning team. To keep the smartest folks teaching, they have to fund their research projects and pay them well, otherwise they’ll go off to private industry and won’t contribute to the up-and-coming generation’s education. If you want to defund education (as you want to defund pretty much everything from what I can tell) go right ahead. Watch all the faculty walk away. Whom you get to replace them is anyones guess, and I’m sure they’ll be working for minimum wage (see what I did there?) without any sort of benefits. I’m sure you’ll have the best of the best teaching the students of this nation. I’m sure they’ll sacrifice for the good of the students. Actually, I think it’d be an epic clusterfuck. As an entropy fan, though, go ahead and bring it on. What’s the worst that could happen?

Nine. And those banks are involved with the corporations. If the capitalists heard you talking like this, you’d be suicided. Business and banks go hand in hand, in the name of liquidity. The fed, whether you like them or loath them, keeps this whole thing afloat. At this point in time they are just trying to make sure that we’re the last ones that collapse.

Ten. No idea what that’s all about, but lets face it, hospitals can’t make a profit on old people whom are on Medicare or Medicaid (because you’d shut down both those programs, I’m sure). Hospitals can’t make a profit on them, so lets face it, it’s bad for shareholders, and so the best course of action is to tell them to go away and die peacefully. Out of sight, out of mind. Profit is the only game in town when it comes to hospitals, and clinics. They have to get their money. Shut down federal programs and see the death rates skyrocket. I’m sure that won’t be reported on, considering that the news corporations are also running for profit and don’t want to paint this issue in a bad light. That’s why the VA doesn’t get any press.

Eleven. I’m fine with that, if you agree to cash everyone out. There’s a database with how much everyone has contributed to social security, medicare, etc. If we gave of that money, and you shut the programs down, I’ll be expecting full reimbursement for the funds I gave that I wouldn’t get to use. Every damn penny.

Twelve. And what sort of taxes do you actually find permissible? Sounds to me like you’re in favor of shutting everything down. I imagine that the moment you mentioned that to the military industrial complex they’d treat you like a Kennedy in rapid fashion.

Ultimately, this is just a thought exercise, and nothing besides. The system will stay exactly the way it is whether you and I agree or disagree. It’s all big business, and they want their flow of funding secured. No one can stop it. Not you. Not me. Not Bernie Sanders. It’s fun to discuss, but at the end of the day, completely pointless. I do wish you well with whatever it is you do for a living, and I hope none of you benefits are taken away, and that you’re not slighted in the least. I’d hope you’d wish me the same, but I’m not so sure. I can hope though. This country was founded on people getting together and shouting at each other, but respecting ones right to shout, especially when they are disagreed with. There’s no point to any of this if we lose that.
